title: Relation registry — bridge mappings (canonical vocabulary ⇄ bridged-project relations)
description: The machine-validated bridge layer of the koine relation registry: how each bridged project's own predicates cross into the canonical node/edge vocabulary — the schema now hosted here in koine (`registry/canonical-schema.json`), with pinakes holding a generated mirror. Lifted from pinakes `shared/predicate-mapping.json` (merged as `17f0713`) into koine as the ecosystem contract — every merged entry preserved as-is, the lift purely additive — koine holds the vocabulary DATA, agora holds the tooling that validates and loads it (ADR-0001; ADR-0002 amendment). It does NOT coin relation names: the relation vocabulary is `relations.tsv` + `relations/<domain>.tsv` in this directory, and every mapping that crosses as a claim names the registry relation it normalizes to (`koineRelations`) — ONE vocabulary, no second source of truth. Encodes ARGOS_SYNC_PLAN.md Appendix A: the Analyzer relations, the `sha256:`/`cs:` id-space rules, the `local-only` class that keeps personal-tier facts from ever leaving the machine (an EGRESS class per KGP §7.2, not a dialect tier — the two axes were split apart at registryVersion 0.3.0, see `axes`), and the `t_start`/`t_end` ⇄ `time_start`/`time_end` temporal-field map. Each relation entry names a canonical node/edge type (validated for totality against the producer's canonical schema) or a non-type mapping (derived rule / provenance columns / temporal fields); a `pending` flag marks declared-but-not-yet-added canonical schema additions, so the flag doubles as a live checklist. The `projects` block covers both bridged projects: analyzer (lifted as merged) and insimul (added additively at registryVersion 0.4.0 from INSIMUL_SYNC_PLAN.md Appendix A + insimul-babylon `packages/core/src/prolog/predicate-schema.ts`; every entry carries the `sourceRow` it came from). pinakes is not listed there — it remains the canonical SIDE of every mapping, so its coverage IS the relation vocabulary and the canonical node/edge schema; but the canonical SCHEMA those `canonicalType` references resolve against is now hosted in koine (`registry/canonical-schema.json`), not pinakes — pinakes keeps a generated mirror.

canonicalHome.tooling: agora — schema, validator and loader library (`20-shared-relation-registry` US-SRR4); koine ships no code
canonicalHome.rule: This file is the only authoritative copy. A consumer loads it from here (over the wire, via the agora loader) or keeps a declared mirror; it never edits a local copy.

mirrors.note: The pre-lift original. It stays byte-derived from this file — regenerated, never hand-edited — so the registry cannot fork; `shared/predicate-mapping.ts` keeps typing it and the pinakes drift gate compares the mirror against this canonical copy. Wiring that regeneration is pinakes tasklist `10-pinakes-koine-align` (this tranche does not touch the projects, per ADR-0002 'Consequences').

relationRegistry.rule: The relation vocabulary lives in those TSVs and nowhere else. A mapping whose `canonicalKind` is `edge` or `derived-rule` crosses as a KGP claim and MUST name at least one relation from them in `koineRelations`; every other kind (node / node-property / provenance / temporal / rule / none) is not a relation and MUST leave `koineRelations` empty. A bridged predicate with no registry relation is closed by adding the relation to the TSV by PR — never by naming it only here.
relationRegistry.spec: KGP §3.2 rule 1 — the registry fixes arity and canonical argument order, so claim ids are not producer-dependent.

signaturePolicy.rule: A relation's signature is immutable once published. Changing arity, argument order or the symmetric flag silently changes every dependent claim id (KGP §3), so a change means a NEW relation name — never an edit to a published row.
signaturePolicy.mappingEntries: A mapping entry's `id` and `external` are likewise stable within a project: retarget by adding an entry and superseding, not by rewriting a published one.
signaturePolicy.enforcedBy: agora — the registry validator diffs signatures across `registryVersion`s (US-SRR4)

axes.rule: THREE orthogonal axes ride on knowledge, and none implies another: `dialect` (what logic a consumer may evaluate), `egress` (whether it may leave at all) and provenance `trust` (how much to believe the source). A relation entry carries `dialect` and `egress` independently; trust is not a registry field.
axes.supersedes: `portabilityClasses` (registryVersion ≤ 0.2.0) bundled the first two into one enum, which read `local-only` as a fourth dialect tier. KGP 0.4.0 ruled it an EGRESS class instead, so 0.3.0 splits the key: the three dialect tiers moved to `dialectTiers`, `local-only` to `egressClasses`, and each relation's `portability: [...]` array became a `dialect` + `egress` pair (`horn-safe`+`local-only` → `dialect: horn-safe`, `egress: local-only`; an entry that named no dialect keeps `dialect: null`).
axes.collision: ADR-0002 'Terminology collisions' — the projects use the word 'tier' for all three. Do not conflate them.

dialectTiers.axis: dialect — what logic a consumer may safely EVALUATE
dialectTiers.rule: A producer ships the lowest tier that carries the needed content; a consumer rejects a pack whose tier exceeds what it can safely evaluate. The tiers nest in the order above, so a `grounding-only` relation is safe in a `horn-safe` pack.

classes.grounding-only: Reference data consumed at ground time; no runtime predicate crosses.
classes.horn-safe: Crosses the boundary into pinakes's constrained-Horn Datalog layer (+ arithmetic after Phase 1).
classes.full-prolog: Full ISO Prolog only (cuts / negation / probabilistic likelihood) — does not cross to Datalog.

egressClasses.axis: egress — whether knowledge may LEAVE its originating tier at all
egressClasses.rule: Enforced in BOTH directions. A producer MUST NOT emit a `local-only` relation or record into a pack that crosses a project boundary — the filter runs at pack construction and is never left to the consumer. A consumer MUST reject a pack that carries one and report it (it means a producer bug or a tampered pack) rather than silently dropping the offending records.
egressClasses.hashing: Because it is enforced at pack construction, egress class does not enter the claim hash (KGP §3.1) and never affects claim identity.

classes.exportable: May cross a project boundary, subject to the licence policy (KGP §7.1) and the dialect tier (§5).
classes.local-only: Never leaves the personal tier. Hard-gated out of open-data releases, packaged corpora, and any non-personal export or training set (the privacy invariant this bridge introduces).

trustTiers.axis: trust — how much to BELIEVE a source. Descriptive, never enforcing
trustTiers.carriedBy: provenance records on the pack, NOT relation entries here — listed only to keep the third axis distinct
trustTiers.note: `personal` typically co-occurs with egress `local-only`, but that is correlation: trust describes where a fact came from, egress decides whether it may move.

idSpaces.description: A content-addressed Analyzer asset (id = sha256 of bytes) → canonical `asset` node. Re-encode changes the hash; `derived-from` lineage partially compensates (registry future-work).
A grounded canonical pinakes entity (csid). The Bridge-1 `refers_to` target: a fact may reference a real-world entity, not only an asset hash.
An Analyzer run. Default: fact provenance only, not a graph node.
A versioned Analyzer EDL take. Default: fact provenance only, not a graph node.

analyzer.title: Analyzer — agentic multimedia studio (the user's file web)

direction.AR->LS: Analyzer predicate → pinakes canonical (Bridge 2: the file web as corpus).
direction.LS->AR: pinakes canonical → Analyzer (Bridge 1: entity grounding + world knowledge).

pendingSchemaAdditions.note: Landed by analyzer-bridge US-003: the `asset` node type + `depicts`/`mentions` edge types now resolve in shared/canonical-schema.json (v1.2.0), so the relation `pending` flags below are flipped to false and these lists are empty. Nothing is pending.

relations.notes: container / duration / codec / width / height sub-facts → asset node properties, not edges.
Vision caption / detected object. Object X may carry an entity_ref (csid) after Bridge-1 grounding.
ASR segments → asset transcript property + temporal facts; t_start/t_end ⇄ time_start/time_end (see temporalFieldMap).
Article / text ingest → asset text property.
Temporal segmentation facts; endpoints map through temporalFieldMap.
A derived rule, never a stored edge — same derived-not-stored discipline as pinakes's temporal edges.
Existing canonical edge type. Lineage transitivity is one Horn rule (US-004).
Bridge-1 grounding: `depicts`/`mentions` with entity_ref = csid. Confidence from the grounding rubric; ambiguous candidates never auto-merged.
US-CS6 constraint facts → rules-registry entries + violation facts. Third instance of the provenanced-rules pattern (pinakes Phase 4b, Insimul validators).
Canonical nodes (culture / place / language / deity / …) exported as the shared GroundingPack format (same schema as the Insimul bridge).

relations.external: fact provenance {source, source_url, retrieved_at, confidence, license}
relations.notes: The US-PL1 alignment — identical field names. `license` is an SPDX id; facts derived from licensed reference data keep the license through the bridge.

insimul.title: Insimul — generated worlds (Babylon/Unity/Unreal/Godot; ISO Prolog world KBs)
insimul.sourceDoc: INSIMUL_SYNC_PLAN.md Appendix A (registry v0 draft) + insimul-babylon `packages/core/src/prolog/predicate-schema.ts` (the shipped Mongo ⇄ Prolog catalog)

direction.IN->LS: Insimul predicate → pinakes canonical (Bridge 2: generated worlds as a synthetic corpus).
direction.LS->IN: pinakes canonical → Insimul (Bridge 1: grounding packs seed a world).
direction.none: Crosses in NEITHER direction. Catalogued anyway so the KGP §7.2 egress filter has an explicit rule for it — see `egress`.

entryFields.sourceRow: The INSIMUL_SYNC_PLAN.md Appendix A row this entry derives from (`—` when it comes from predicate-schema.ts alone). Appendix A rows that bundle a node and its edges are split into one entry per `canonicalKind`, so ids are registry-local and do NOT match row numbers.
entryFields.external: The predicate(s) Insimul actually emits, as named in predicate-schema.ts — not the draft's names where the two disagree (see `collisions`).

idSpace.form: sanitized MongoDB ObjectId atom, scoped to one world
idSpace.rule: An Insimul entity id is unique within a world, NOT across worlds or projects, so it is not a KINP id and MUST NOT cross a boundary as one. Bridge 1 persists a csid → seeded-entity map per world (idempotent re-import); Bridge 2 mints canonical ids (`cs:`) on export and carries `world_id` + generation seed as provenance. See INSIMUL_SYNC_PLAN §7 'Identity'.

pendingSchemaAdditions.note: Landed by insimul-bridge US-003: the `character` / `building` / `business` node types and the `parent-of` / `spouse-of` / `employed-by` / `resides-in` / `caused-by` edge types now resolve in pinakes `shared/canonical-schema.json` (v1.3.0), so the relation `pending` flags below are flipped to false and these lists are empty. Nothing is pending. Endpoint note for `caused-by` (entry 12): a truth event still has no canonical node type of its own, so Bridge 2 anchors truths on the canonical type this registry already pairs them with (`myth-motif`, entry 6) and the edge stays endpoint-unconstrained in the schema.

collisions.rule: Reported and resolved here rather than silently reconciled in an entry (ADR-0002 'Terminology collisions'). Analyzer entries above were left exactly as merged; the insimul block is purely additive.
resolved: `settlement` is not a canonical node type — pinakes models settlements as `place` ('A geographic place, settlement, or site'). Entry 2 targets `place`; Appendix A's node name was a draft convenience.

Appendix A row 9 writes `spouse_of/2`; the shipped predicate is `married_to/2` (predicate-schema.ts, character block). `external` names what the producer emits, so the entry says `married_to/2` — and the registry relation is `soc:spouse_of`, which is where the draft's name survives.

`child_of/2` is NOT a second relation. `soc:parent_of` fixes the canonical argument order (parent, child) and names `soc:child_of` as its `inverse`; a producer emitting `child_of/2` normalizes by swapping arguments (KGP §3.2 rule 1), never by coining a relation.

Analyzer's lineage relation is `derived_from` (an artifact derives from a source); Insimul's is genealogical (`descended_from`, descendant→ancestor). Distinct relations, deliberately not merged — collapsing them would let a re-encode license a claim about ancestry.

`located_in` vs core `part_of`: `at_location/2` places a person at a location, which is positional, not mereological. Closed by adding `located_in` to `relations.tsv` rather than by overloading `part_of`.
Insimul's `truth` is a world fact, NOT a KGP claim and NOT a provenance trust tier; its `truth_public/1` flag is a story-visibility flag and says nothing about egress.

relations.notes: Real government / social-structure fields seed `countries.governmentType` etc. Reference data at ground time; no runtime predicate crosses. `country_name/2` added at 0.4.1: a Bridge-1 seed with no name is unusable, and the predicate is in the shipped catalog (predicate-schema.ts `country` block) — the v0 draft simply omitted it.

Coordinates are real; Insimul lays out lots and streets procedurally around them (they ride on the pack's entity `fields`, not as a predicate — the settlement block has no coordinate predicate). Canonical type is `place`, not `settlement` (see `collisions`). `settlement_name/2` added at 0.4.1, same reason as entry 1.

`WorldLanguage` + vocabulary + CEFR text-generation constraints. Feeds the language-learning vertical; conlang generation is grounded in real typology. `language_real_code/2` is the tie back to the canonical language node (ISO code).

relations.external: religion truths / backstory templates (deity + syncretism seeds)
relations.notes: The canonical `syncretized-with` edge seeds template selection at ground time; it does NOT cross as a claim, which is why `koineRelations` is empty. If a bridge ever ships it as an edge, add the relation to the TSVs first.

relations.external: item/1, item_name/2, item_type/2, item_base_type/2, item_is_a/2, item_category/2
relations.notes: Cuisines / ingredients / cooking techniques seed the item taxonomy. `item_is_a/2` (baseType IS-A) is the same shape as core `instance_of`, but it is derived inside the world at sync time and does not cross; an IN->LS export of the taxonomy would be an `instance_of` edge entry of its own. `item_name/2` added at 0.4.1, same reason as entry 1.

relations.external: truth/3 + backstory templates, Tracery `truthBindings`, narrative/2 story templates
relations.notes: Motifs seed authored truth / narrative templates (`narratives` collection, stored prologContent).
Positional containment in a place. `located_in` was added to `relations.tsv` for this entry (positional, not mereological — see `collisions`).
Canonical argument order is (descendant, ancestor) on both sides. The ancestor closure is derived by one Horn rule, never stored pairwise.

relations.external: person/1, first_name/2, last_name/2, birth_year/2, gender/2, alive/1, occupation/2
relations.notes: Bridge 2. Landed as the canonical `character` node type (`Character`) in pinakes canonical schema v1.3.0 — the vocabulary's first person-family type. Generated persons, so `synthetic` trust — which is a provenance property, not an egress one: they are exportable.
`child_of/2` normalizes to the same relation with arguments swapped (KGP §3.2 rule 1); it is the declared `inverse`, not a second relation.

`soc:spouse_of` is symmetric, so operands are sorted before hashing (KGP §3.2 rule 2) and the two directions Insimul stores collapse to one claim. Appendix A called the predicate `spouse_of/2` (see `collisions`).

Event causality, canonical order (effect, cause) — high value for multi-hop QA synthesis, because a generated world ships its complete causal chain (no KB-incompleteness noise). Landed as the `caused-by` edge type in pinakes canonical schema v1.3.0, endpoint-UNCONSTRAINED: a truth event has no canonical node type of its own, so Bridge 2 anchors each truth on `myth-motif` (the type entry 6 already pairs Insimul truths with) rather than coining an `event` type. Insimul does not yet ship `causesTruthIds`/`causedByTruthIds` on `TruthIR` — the fields are declared by INSIMUL_SYNC_PLAN Appendix A row 10 and read forward-compatibly by the pinakes adapter, which emits no causality edge when they are absent.

relations.external: business/1, business_type/2, lot/1, lot_building/2, lot_building_type/2, residence/1
relations.notes: Bridge 2; both node types landed in pinakes canonical schema v1.3.0 (`Building` / `Business`). A lot's building is the `building` node (the lot itself is not a canonical entity — its address / block ride as node properties).
`occupation/2` is a job title (a node property), not an employer — only owner/founder edges carry an employer id today; a general employment predicate is an Insimul-side gap.
Occupancy, distinct from `located_in` (a resident dwells there; a character standing there is merely positioned).

A truth is a point event: `truth_year` becomes both canonical endpoints. `truth_timestep` is world-internal ordering and `current_year/1` is engine state — neither has a canonical counterpart. Contemporary / precedes are DERIVED on both sides, never stored pairwise (same discipline as pinakes's temporal edges and analyzer entry 6).

Insimul runs full ISO Prolog (tau/Trealla): cuts, negation and `rule_likelihood/2` random-chance patterns do NOT cross to pinakes's constrained-Horn layer. Only the horn-safe subset crosses, checked by shared golden conformance cases; a ProbLog emitter can carry likelihood as a fact probability. This is the third instance of the provenanced-rules pattern (pinakes Phase 4b, analyzer entry 9).

relations.external: truth.source, citations, radiant_generated/3, world_id + generation seed
relations.notes: Bridge-2 output lands in the `synthetic` trust tier with `world_id` + generation seed as provenance and the license marked proprietary — never mixed into open-data releases (INSIMUL_SYNC_PLAN §7 'License leakage'). Trust tier ≠ egress class.

A REAL person's language-learning performance and chat turns (predicate-schema.ts `cefrProficiency`; the `languagechatmessages` / `playthroughs` collections). Never a world fact and never a canonical node — catalogued solely so the KGP §7.2 filter has an explicit rule: the producer drops these at pack construction and a consumer rejects-and-reports a pack that still carries them. This is the Insimul counterpart of analyzer's personal-tier file facts.
